content.intro: Learn deleting records efficiently through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines deleting records efficiently as part of the django orm and querysets. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Instance deletion; QuerySet deletion; Cascade behavior; Deletion signals; Protecting important related records. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Instance deletion
items.text: For Instance deletion, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: QuerySet deletion
items.text: A QuerySet describes database operations and is commonly lazy. Build filters and ordering before evaluation; use the database to narrow results rather than pulling everything into Python.

items.title: Cascade behavior
items.text: For Cascade behavior, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: Deletion signals
items.text: Signals allow decoupled listeners but can hide control flow. Use them for genuinely cross-cutting hooks, register receivers predictably, and consider a direct function call for core business steps.

items.title: Protecting important related records
items.text: Protecting important related records affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.
